verses.tsw_comparator: When they make a long blast with the ram’s horn, when you hear the sound of the horn, all the people shall shout with a great shout. Then the wall of the city shall fall beneath itself, and the people shall go up, each straight ahead.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated seven-priest instruction and both ark titles.
verses.before: So Joshua son of Nun called the priests and said to them, “Take up the ark of the covenant, and let seven priests carry seven ram’s horns before the ark of the LORD.”
verses.after: Joshua son of Nun called the priests and told them, “Lift the ark of the covenant. Seven priests are to carry seven ram’s horns ahead of the ark of the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So Joshua son of Nun called the priests and said to them, “Take up the ark of the covenant, and let seven priests carry seven ram’s horns before the ark of the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Follows the qere singular he said with Joshua as speaker; notes the written plural without changing the order of march.
verses.before: He said to the people, “Pass on and march around the city, and let the armed men pass before the ark of the LORD.”
verses.after: Then he told the people, “Move out and march around the city. Let the armed men go ahead of the ark of the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to the people, “Pass on and march around the city, and let the armed men pass before the ark of the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the simultaneous command/action and the sequence priests then ark.
verses.before: When Joshua had spoken to the people, the seven priests carrying the seven ram’s horns before the LORD passed on and blew the horns, and the ark of the covenant of the LORD followed them.
verses.after: As Joshua spoke to the people, the seven priests carrying seven ram’s horns before the LORD moved out, blowing the horns. The ark of the LORD’s covenant followed them.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Joshua had spoken to the people, the seven priests carrying the seven ram’s horns before the LORD passed on and blew the horns, and the ark of the covenant of the LORD followed them.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes vanguard, priests, ark, and rear guard without assigning horn blowing to the rear guard.
verses.before: The armed men went before the priests who blew the horns, and the rear guard followed the ark while the horns continued sounding.
verses.after: The armed men marched ahead of the priests blowing the horns, and the rear guard followed the ark, while the horns kept sounding.
verses.tsw_comparator: The armed men went before the priests who blew the horns, and the rear guard followed the ark while the horns continued sounding.

verses.rationale: Preserves the threefold silence command and precise release cue.
verses.before: Joshua commanded the people, saying, “You will not shout or let your voice be heard, nor will any word go out of your mouth until the day I say to you, ‘Shout!’ Then you will shout.”
verses.after: Joshua had commanded the people, “Do not shout or let your voices be heard. Do not let a word leave your mouths until the day I tell you, ‘Shout!’ Then shout.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua commanded the people, saying, “You shall not shout or let your voice be heard, nor shall any word go out of your mouth until the day I say to you, ‘Shout!’ Then you shall shout.”

verses.rationale: Retains Joshua’s causative role, single circuit, and overnight return.
verses.before: So he caused the ark of the LORD to circle the city, going around it once. Then they entered the camp and spent the night in the camp.
verses.after: He had the ark of the LORD circle the city once. Then they returned to camp and spent the night there.
verses.tsw_comparator: So he caused the ark of the LORD to circle the city, going around it once. Then they entered the camp and spent the night in the camp.

verses.rationale: Keeps early rising and the priests’ action as the next circuit begins.
verses.before: Joshua rose early in the morning, and the priests took up the ark of the LORD.
verses.after: Joshua rose early the next morning, and the priests lifted the ark of the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua rose early in the morning, and the priests took up the ark of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains the deliberate repetition of the full procession and continuous horn sound.
verses.before: The seven priests carrying the seven ram’s horns before the ark of the LORD walked on, continually blowing the horns. The armed men went before them, and the rear guard followed the ark of the LORD, while the horns continued sounding.
verses.after: The seven priests carrying seven ram’s horns ahead of the ark of the LORD kept marching and blowing. The armed men went ahead of them, and the rear guard followed the ark of the LORD, while the horns kept sounding.
verses.tsw_comparator: The seven priests carrying the seven ram’s horns before the ark of the LORD walked on, continually blowing the horns. The armed men went before them, and the rear guard followed the ark of the LORD, while the horns continued sounding.

verses.rationale: Preserves the second-day detail and six-day summary without collapsing their sequence.
verses.before: On the second day they circled the city once and returned to the camp. Thus they did six days.
verses.after: On the second day they circled the city once and returned to camp. They did this for six days.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the second day they circled the city once and returned to the camp. Thus they did six days.

verses.rationale: Keeps the dawn start and emphatic repetition that distinguishes the seventh day.
verses.before: On the seventh day they rose early at the dawning of the day and circled the city in the same manner seven times. Only on that day did they circle the city seven times.
verses.after: On the seventh day they rose at dawn and circled the city in the same way seven times. Only on that day did they circle it seven times.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the seventh day they rose early at the dawning of the day and circled the city in the same manner seven times. Only on that day did they circle the city seven times.

verses.rationale: Preserves the cue’s fulfillment and Joshua’s gift declaration.
verses.before: At the seventh time, when the priests blew the horns, Joshua said to the people, “Shout, for the LORD has given you the city!
verses.after: On the seventh circuit, when the priests blew the horns, Joshua told the people, “Shout! The LORD has given you the city!
verses.tsw_comparator: At the seventh time, when the priests blew the horns, Joshua said to the people, “Shout, for the LORD has given you the city!

verses.rationale: Makes herem’s lethal consequence explicit while retaining divine dedication and the stated exception and reason.
verses.before: The city and all that is in it will be devoted to destruction for the LORD. Only Rahab the prostitute will live, she and everyone who are with her in the house, because she hid the messengers whom we sent.
verses.after: The city and everything in it are devoted to the LORD for destruction. Only Rahab the prostitute and everyone with her in the house are to live, because she hid the messengers we sent.
verses.tsw_comparator: The city and all that is in it shall be devoted to destruction for the LORD. Only Rahab the prostitute shall live, she and all who are with her in the house, because she hid the messengers whom we sent.

verses.rationale: Unfolds the difficult repeated herem clause and preserves the corporate danger; notes alternate understanding of incur destruction.
verses.before: But as for you, keep yourselves from what is devoted to destruction, lest you desire and take from what is devoted and make the camp of Israel itself devoted to destruction and bring trouble upon it.
verses.after: But keep away from what is devoted to destruction. If you take any of it while carrying out the destruction, you will make Israel’s camp itself subject to destruction and bring trouble on it.
verses.tsw_comparator: But as for you, keep yourselves from what is devoted to destruction, lest you desire and take from what is devoted and make the camp of Israel itself devoted to destruction and bring trouble upon it.

verses.rationale: Keeps the four metals and their distinct treasury disposition rather than treating them as ordinary spoil.
verses.before: All the silver and gold, and vessels of bronze and iron, are holy to the LORD. They will come into the treasury of the LORD.”
verses.after: All silver and gold, and all objects of bronze and iron, are holy to the LORD. They must go into the LORD’s treasury.”
verses.tsw_comparator: All the silver and gold, and vessels of bronze and iron, are holy to the LORD. They shall come into the treasury of the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the doubled shout report and straight-ahead entry without smoothing away the narrative repetition.
verses.before: So the people shouted, and the priests blew the horns. When the people heard the sound of the horn, the people shouted with a great shout, and the wall fell beneath itself. The people went up into the city, each straight ahead, and they captured the city.
verses.after: The people shouted, and the horns sounded. When the people heard the horn blast, they gave a great shout, and the wall fell down where it stood. They went up into the city, each straight ahead, and captured it.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the people shouted, and the priests blew the horns. When the people heard the sound of the horn, the people shouted with a great shout, and the wall fell beneath itself. The people went up into the city, each straight ahead, and they captured the city.

verses.rationale: Names the human and animal victims and the killing explicitly, retaining herem rather than euphemistic victory.
verses.before: They devoted to destruction all that was in the city, from man to woman, from young to old, and ox and sheep and donkey, with the edge of the sword.
verses.after: They devoted everything in the city to destruction, killing with the sword men and women, young and old, cattle, sheep, and donkeys.
verses.tsw_comparator: They devoted to destruction all that was in the city, from man to woman, from young to old, and ox and sheep and donkey, with the edge of the sword.

verses.rationale: Keeps the spies responsible for fulfilling their own oath and the household scope.
verses.before: Joshua said to the two men who had spied out the land, “Go into the prostitute’s house and bring out from there the woman and everyone who belong to her, as you swore to her.”
verses.after: Joshua told the two men who had spied out the land, “Go into the prostitute’s house. Bring out the woman and all who belong to her, just as you swore to her.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua said to the two men who had spied out the land, “Go into the prostitute’s house and bring out from there the woman and all who belong to her, as you swore to her.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the extended family, repeated rescue action, and initial placement outside the camp.
verses.before: So the young men who had been spies went in and brought out Rahab, her father, her mother, her brothers, and everyone who belonged to her. They brought out all her clan and placed them outside the camp of Israel.
verses.after: The young spies went in and brought out Rahab, her father and mother, her brothers, and all who belonged to her. They brought out all her relatives and settled them outside Israel’s camp.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the young men who had been spies went in and brought out Rahab, her father, her mother, her brothers, and all who belonged to her. They brought out all her clan and placed them outside the camp of Israel.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes burning from the four-metal exception and retains the LORD’s house title.
verses.before: They burned the city with fire and all that was in it. Only the silver and gold and vessels of bronze and iron they put into the treasury of the house of the LORD.
verses.after: They burned the city and everything in it. Only the silver, gold, and objects of bronze and iron went into the treasury of the LORD’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: They burned the city with fire and all that was in it. Only the silver and gold and vessels of bronze and iron they put into the treasury of the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains the singular she and narrator’s to-this-day perspective without turning it into an unsupported claim about descendants.
verses.before: Yet Rahab the prostitute, her father’s household, and everyone who belonged to her Joshua preserved alive. She has lived among Israel to this day because she hid the messengers whom Joshua sent to spy out Jericho.
verses.after: But Joshua spared Rahab the prostitute, her father’s household, and all who belonged to her. She has lived among Israel to this day, because she hid the messengers Joshua sent to spy out Jericho.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Rahab the prostitute, her father’s household, and all who belonged to her Joshua preserved alive. She has lived in the midst of Israel to this day because she hid the messengers whom Joshua sent to spy out Jericho.

verses.rationale: Preserves the oath-curse and parallel firstborn/youngest cost in poetic lines, without specifying a mechanism of death.
verses.before: Joshua made them swear at that time, saying: “Cursed before the LORD is the man who rises and rebuilds this city, Jericho. At the cost of his firstborn he will lay its foundation, and at the cost of his youngest he will set up its gates.”
verses.after: At that time Joshua imposed this oath: “Cursed before the LORD is the man who rises to rebuild this city, Jericho! At the cost of his firstborn he will lay its foundation; at the cost of his youngest he will set up its gates.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua made them swear at that time, saying: “Cursed before the LORD is the man who rises and rebuilds this city, Jericho. At the cost of his firstborn he shall lay its foundation, and at the cost of his youngest he shall set up its gates.”

verses.rationale: Retains the divine-presence conclusion and geographical spread of Joshua’s reputation.
verses.before: So the LORD was with Joshua, and his fame was throughout all the land.
verses.after: The LORD was with Joshua, and his fame spread throughout the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the LORD was with Joshua, and his fame was throughout all the land.

verses.rationale: Preserves the movement from Israel’s collective breach to Achan’s act and back to divine anger against Israel; keeps the full lineage.
verses.before: But the children of Israel acted unfaithfully concerning what was devoted. Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, from the tribe of Judah, took from what was devoted, and the anger of the LORD burned against the children of Israel.
verses.after: But the Israelites broke faith concerning what was devoted to destruction. Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, from the tribe of Judah, took some of it, and the LORD’s anger burned against the Israelites.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the children of Israel acted unfaithfully concerning what was devoted. Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, from the tribe of Judah, took from what was devoted, and the anger of the LORD burned against the children of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains both nearby place names, eastward relation, and command/fulfillment repetition.
verses.before: Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which is near Beth-Aven, east of Bethel, and said to them, “Go up and spy out the land.” The men went up and spied out Ai.
verses.after: Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, near Beth-aven, east of Bethel. “Go up and spy out the land,” he told them. They went up and spied out Ai.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which is near Beth-Aven, east of Bethel, and said to them, “Go up and spy out the land.” The men went up and spied out Ai.

verses.rationale: Keeps the alternative approximate troop counts and identifies the few as Ai’s people rather than Israel’s.
verses.before: They returned to Joshua and said to him, “Do not let all the people go up. Let about two or three thousand men go up and strike Ai. Do not weary all the people there, for they are few.”
verses.after: They returned to Joshua and said, “Not all the people need to go up. Let about two or three thousand men go up and strike Ai. Do not wear everyone out going there; there are only a few people in Ai.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They returned to Joshua and said to him, “Do not let all the people go up. Let about two or three thousand men go up and strike Ai. Do not weary all the people there, for they are few.”

verses.rationale: Preserves approximate deployment and the abrupt reversal of expectation.
verses.before: So about three thousand men from the people went up there, but they fled before the men of Ai.
verses.after: About three thousand men went up there, but they fled from the men of Ai.
verses.tsw_comparator: So about three thousand men from the people went up there, but they fled before the men of Ai.

verses.rationale: Keeps approximate casualties, the uncertain place name, and the heart-to-water image that reverses the enemy’s fear.
verses.before: The men of Ai struck about thirty-six men of them. They pursued them from before the gate as far as Shebarim and struck them on the descent. Then the hearts of the people melted and became like water.
verses.after: The men of Ai killed about thirty-six of them, chasing them from the gate as far as Shebarim and striking them down on the descent. The people’s hearts melted and turned to water.
verses.tsw_comparator: The men of Ai struck about thirty-six men of them. They pursued them from before the gate as far as Shebarim and struck them on the descent. Then the hearts of the people melted and became like water.

verses.rationale: Preserves the public mourning gestures, companions, location, and duration.
verses.before: Joshua tore his clothes and fell on his face to the ground before the ark of the LORD until evening, he and the elders of Israel. They put dust on their heads.
verses.after: Joshua tore his clothes and fell facedown to the ground before the ark of the LORD, along with the elders of Israel. They stayed there until evening and put dust on their heads.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua tore his clothes and fell on his face to the ground before the ark of the LORD until evening, he and the elders of Israel. They put dust on their heads.

verses.rationale: Retains Joshua’s accusatory question and wish without correcting or softening his protest.
verses.before: Joshua said, “Ah, Lord GOD! Why did you ever bring this people across the Jordan, only to give us into the hand of the Amorites to destroy us? If only we had been content to remain beyond the Jordan!
verses.after: Joshua said, “Ah, Lord GOD! Why did you ever bring these people across the Jordan—to hand us over to the Amorites and destroy us? If only we had been content to stay on the other side of the Jordan!
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua said, “Ah, Lord GOD! Why did you ever bring this people across the Jordan, only to give us into the hand of the Amorites to destroy us? If only we had been content to remain beyond the Jordan!

verses.rationale: Keeps the bodily retreat image and rhetorical question in the lament.
verses.before: Please, Lord, what can I say after Israel has turned its back before its enemies?
verses.after: Please, Lord, what can I say now that Israel has turned its back on its enemies?
verses.tsw_comparator: Please, Lord, what can I say after Israel has turned its back before its enemies?

verses.rationale: Preserves the link between Israel’s threatened name and the LORD’s great name.
verses.before: The Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land will hear and surround us and cut off our name from the earth. And what will you do for your great name?”
verses.after: The Canaanites and everyone else in the land will hear. They will surround us and cut off our name from the earth. Then what will you do for your great name?”
verses.tsw_comparator: The Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land will hear and surround us and cut off our name from the earth. And what will you do for your great name?”

verses.rationale: Makes the abrupt divine interruption and question audible.
verses.before: The LORD said to Joshua, “Rise! Why is it that you have fallen on your face?
verses.after: The LORD answered Joshua, “Get up! Why are you lying facedown like this?
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Joshua, “Rise! Why is it that you have fallen on your face?

verses.rationale: Retains the accumulating charges and collective pronouns instead of limiting the divine indictment to Achan.
verses.before: Israel has sinned. They have also transgressed my covenant that I commanded them. They have taken from what was devoted, and they have stolen, and they have deceived, and they have put it among their own goods.
verses.after: Israel has sinned. They have violated my covenant, which I commanded them to keep. They have taken what was devoted to destruction; they have stolen, they have lied, and they have put it among their own belongings.
verses.tsw_comparator: Israel has sinned. They have also transgressed my covenant that I commanded them. They have taken from what was devoted, and they have stolen, and they have deceived, and they have put it among their own goods.

verses.rationale: Keeps the corporate herem reversal and conditional withdrawal of presence with the repeated destruction term.
verses.before: So the children of Israel cannot stand before their enemies. They turn their backs before their enemies because they have become devoted to destruction. I will not continue to be with you unless you destroy what is devoted from among you.
verses.after: That is why the Israelites cannot stand against their enemies. They turn their backs on them because they themselves have become devoted to destruction. I will no longer be with you unless you destroy what is devoted to destruction from among you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore the children of Israel cannot stand before their enemies. They turn their backs before their enemies because they have become devoted to destruction. I will not continue to be with you unless you destroy what is devoted from among you.

verses.rationale: Connects consecration with the next day’s inquiry and retains the repeated among-you language.
verses.before: Rise, consecrate the people and say, ‘Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, for thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: There is something devoted in your midst, Israel. You cannot stand before your enemies until you remove what is devoted from your midst.
verses.after: Get up and consecrate the people. Tell them, ‘Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, for the LORD, the God of Israel, says: There is something devoted to destruction among you, Israel. You cannot stand against your enemies until you remove it from among you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Rise, consecrate the people and say, ‘Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, for thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: There is something devoted in your midst, Israel. You cannot stand before your enemies until you remove what is devoted from your midst.

verses.rationale: Makes the narrowing sequence clear without inserting an unmentioned physical lot procedure.
verses.before: In the morning you will draw near by your tribes. The tribe that the LORD takes will draw near by clans; the clan that the LORD takes will draw near by households; and the household that the LORD takes will draw near man by man.
verses.after: In the morning, present yourselves tribe by tribe. The tribe the LORD singles out must come forward clan by clan; the clan he singles out, household by household; and the household he singles out, man by man.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the morning you shall draw near by your tribes. The tribe that the LORD takes shall draw near by clans; the clan that the LORD takes shall draw near by households; and the household that the LORD takes shall draw near man by man.

verses.rationale: Preserves the burning, encompassing scope, covenant offense, and outrage without prematurely restricting its referents.
verses.before: The one who is taken with what is devoted will be burned with fire, he and all that belongs to him, because he has transgressed the covenant of the LORD and because he has done a disgraceful thing in Israel.’”
verses.after: The one singled out with what was devoted to destruction must be burned with fire, he and everything that belongs to him, because he has violated the LORD’s covenant and committed an outrage in Israel.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: The one who is taken with what is devoted shall be burned with fire, he and all that belongs to him, because he has transgressed the covenant of the LORD and because he has done a disgraceful thing in Israel.’”

verses.rationale: Keeps the first stage of the inquiry and its result.
verses.before: So Joshua rose early in the morning and brought Israel near by tribes, and the tribe of Judah was taken.
verses.after: Joshua rose early in the morning and brought Israel forward tribe by tribe. The tribe of Judah was singled out.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Joshua rose early in the morning and brought Israel near by tribes, and the tribe of Judah was taken.

verses.rationale: Preserves the actual man-by-man wording rather than harmonizing this stage with verse 14’s household instruction.
verses.before: He brought the clans of Judah near, and the clan of the Zerahites was taken. He brought the clan of the Zerahites near man by man, and Zabdi was taken.
verses.after: He brought forward the clans of Judah, and the Zerahite clan was singled out. He brought the Zerahite clan forward man by man, and Zabdi was singled out.
verses.tsw_comparator: He brought the clans of Judah near, and the clan of the Zerahites was taken. He brought the clan of the Zerahites near man by man, and Zabdi was taken.

verses.rationale: Names the household referent and repeats Achan’s complete lineage as the narrative does.
verses.before: He brought his household near man by man, and Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, from the tribe of Judah, was taken.
verses.after: He brought Zabdi’s household forward man by man, and Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, from the tribe of Judah, was singled out.
verses.tsw_comparator: He brought his household near man by man, and Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, from the tribe of Judah, was taken.

verses.rationale: Retains the familial address and glory/confession idiom while making the demand for disclosure plain.
verses.before: Joshua said to Achan, “My son, please give glory to the LORD, the God of Israel, and give him praise. Tell me now what you have done; do not hide it from me.”
verses.after: Joshua said to Achan, “My son, give glory to the LORD, the God of Israel, and acknowledge him. Tell me what you have done; do not hide it from me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua said to Achan, “My son, please give glory to the LORD, the God of Israel, and give him praise. Tell me now what you have done; do not hide it from me.”

verses.rationale: Keeps confession addressed to Joshua and the full divine title before the detailed account.
verses.before: Achan answered Joshua and said, “Truly I have sinned against the LORD, the God of Israel, and this is what I did:
verses.after: Achan answered Joshua, “It is true. I have sinned against the LORD, the God of Israel. This is what I did:
verses.tsw_comparator: Achan answered Joshua and said, “Truly I have sinned against the LORD, the God of Israel, and this is what I did:

verses.rationale: Preserves saw/coveted/took, Shinar, both weights, and the gold-tongue image; leaves underneath’s precise object for the note.
verses.before: When I saw among the plunder a beautiful cloak from Shinar, two hundred shekels of silver, and one bar of gold weighing fifty shekels, I desired them and took them. Look, they are hidden in the ground inside my tent, with the silver underneath.”
verses.after: Among the plunder I saw a beautiful cloak from Shinar, two hundred shekels of silver, and a tongue-shaped bar of gold weighing fifty shekels. I coveted them and took them. They are buried in the ground inside my tent, with the silver underneath.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When I saw among the plunder a beautiful cloak from Shinar, two hundred shekels of silver, and one bar of gold weighing fifty shekels, I desired them and took them. Look, they are hidden in the ground inside my tent, with the silver underneath.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the discovery’s echo of Achan’s description and the hurried verification.
verses.before: So Joshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent. Look, it was hidden in his tent, with the silver underneath.
verses.after: Joshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent. There it was, buried in his tent, with the silver underneath.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Joshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent. Look, it was hidden in his tent, with the silver underneath.

verses.rationale: Retains public presentation before both Israel and the LORD without reducing it to a private discovery.
verses.before: They took them from the midst of the tent, brought them to Joshua and all the children of Israel, and poured them out before the LORD.
verses.after: They took the things out of the tent, brought them to Joshua and all the Israelites, and spread them out before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: They took them from the midst of the tent, brought them to Joshua and all the children of Israel, and poured them out before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves children, animals, possessions, collective participation, and the shortened ancestry as written; assigns no unstated guilt to the children.
verses.before: Joshua and all Israel with him took Achan son of Zerah, the silver, the cloak, the bar of gold, his sons and daughters, his oxen, donkeys, sheep, tent, and all that he had, and brought them up to the Valley of Achor.
verses.after: Joshua, with all Israel, took Achan son of Zerah, the silver, the cloak, the tongue-shaped gold bar, his sons and daughters, his cattle, donkey, sheep, tent, and everything he had. They brought them up to the Valley of Achor.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua and all Israel with him took Achan son of Zerah, the silver, the cloak, the bar of gold, his sons and daughters, his oxen, donkeys, sheep, tent, and all that he had, and brought them up to the Valley of Achor.

verses.rationale: Keeps the shift from singular him to plural them and the narrated order instead of harmonizing away the punishment’s troubling scope.
verses.before: Joshua said, “Why have you brought trouble upon us? The LORD will bring trouble upon you this day.” Then all Israel stoned him with stones. They burned them with fire and stoned them with stones.
verses.after: Joshua said, “Why have you brought trouble on us? The LORD will bring trouble on you today.” All Israel stoned him. They burned them with fire and pelted them with stones.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua said, “Why have you brought trouble upon us? The LORD will bring trouble upon you this day.” Then all Israel stoned him with stones. They burned them with fire and stoned them with stones.

verses.rationale: Preserves the return to singular him, double to-this-day notices, and trouble/Achor wordplay in a note.
verses.before: They raised over him a great heap of stones that remains to this day. Then the LORD turned from his burning anger. Therefore the name of that place was called the Valley of Achor to this day.
verses.after: They raised a great heap of stones over him, which remains to this day. Then the LORD turned from his burning anger. That is why the place is called the Valley of Achor to this day.
verses.tsw_comparator: They raised over him a great heap of stones that remains to this day. Then the LORD turned from his burning anger. Therefore the name of that place was called the Valley of Achor to this day.

verses.rationale: Retains renewed courage, all-troops contrast with chapter 7, and the four objects of the promise.
verses.before: The LORD said to Joshua, “Do not fear and do not be dismayed. Take with you all the people of war, arise, and go up to Ai. See, I have given into your hand the king of Ai, his people, his city, and his land.
verses.after: The LORD told Joshua, “Do not be afraid or discouraged. Take all the fighting men with you and go up to Ai. Look! I have given Ai’s king, people, city, and land into your hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Joshua, “Do not fear and do not be dismayed. Take with you all the people of war, arise, and go up to Ai. See, I have given into your hand the king of Ai, his people, his city, and his land.

verses.rationale: Keeps lethal Jericho comparison and explicitly distinguishes permitted plunder from the former prohibition.
verses.before: You will do to Ai and its king as you did to Jericho and its king, except that its plunder and livestock you may take for yourselves. Set an ambush for the city behind it.”
verses.after: Do to Ai and its king what you did to Jericho and its king. But this time you may take its plunder and livestock for yourselves. Set an ambush behind the city.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall do to Ai and its king as you did to Jericho and its king, except that its plunder and livestock you may take for yourselves. Set an ambush for the city behind it.”

verses.rationale: Preserves thirty thousand without harmonizing it to the five thousand later in the account.
verses.before: So Joshua arose, and all the people of war, to go up to Ai. Joshua chose thirty thousand mighty warriors and sent them out by night.
verses.after: Joshua and all the fighting men set out to go up to Ai. Joshua chose thirty thousand mighty warriors and sent them out at night.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Joshua arose, and all the people of war, to go up to Ai. Joshua chose thirty thousand mighty warriors and sent them out by night.

verses.rationale: Keeps the attention cue, concealment location, proximity limit, and readiness command.
verses.before: He commanded them, saying, “See, you are to lie in ambush against the city, behind the city. Do not go very far from the city, and all of you be ready.
verses.after: He commanded them, “Listen. You are to lie in ambush behind the city. Do not go too far from it, and all of you be ready.
verses.tsw_comparator: He commanded them, saying, “See, you are to lie in ambush against the city, behind the city. Do not go very far from the city, and all of you be ready.

verses.rationale: Makes the two forces distinct while retaining the planned echo of the earlier defeat.
verses.before: I and all the people who are with me will draw near to the city. When they come out against us as at the first, we will flee before them.
verses.after: I and all the people with me will approach the city. When they come out against us as they did before, we will flee from them.
verses.tsw_comparator: I and all the people who are with me will draw near to the city. When they come out against us as at the first, we will flee before them.

verses.rationale: Keeps both the enemy’s predicted interpretation and the repeated planned flight across a verse boundary.
verses.before: They will come out after us until we have drawn them away from the city, for they will say, ‘They are fleeing before us as at the first.’ So we will flee before them.
verses.after: They will come after us until we have drawn them away from the city. They will say, ‘They are running from us just as before!’ As we flee from them,
verses.tsw_comparator: They will come out after us until we have drawn them away from the city, for they will say, ‘They are fleeing before us as at the first.’ So we will flee before them.

verses.rationale: Connects the ambush force’s action with the promise while retaining the hands image.
verses.before: Then you will rise from the ambush and take possession of the city, and the LORD your God will give it into your hand.
verses.after: you are to rise from the ambush and seize the city. The LORD your God will give it into your hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then you shall rise from the ambush and take possession of the city, and the LORD your God will give it into your hand.

verses.rationale: Preserves capture-before-burning and both divine word and Joshua’s command.
verses.before: When you have captured the city, set the city on fire. According to the word of the LORD you will do. See, I have commanded you.”
verses.after: Once you have captured the city, set it on fire. Do as the LORD has said. See that you carry out my command.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When you have captured the city, set the city on fire. According to the word of the LORD you shall do. See, I have commanded you.”

verses.rationale: Retains Bethel/Ai and westward placement, with Joshua’s distinct overnight location.
verses.before: Joshua sent them out, and they went to the place of ambush and stayed between Bethel and Ai, west of Ai. But Joshua spent that night among the people.
verses.after: Joshua sent them out, and they took their ambush position between Bethel and Ai, west of Ai. Joshua spent that night among the people.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua sent them out, and they went to the place of ambush and stayed between Bethel and Ai, west of Ai. But Joshua spent that night among the people.

verses.rationale: Keeps mustering, elders, and leadership at the front of the advance.
verses.before: Joshua rose early in the morning, mustered the people, and went up, he and the elders of Israel, before the people to Ai.
verses.after: Early the next morning Joshua mustered the people. He and the elders of Israel went ahead of them up to Ai.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua rose early in the morning, mustered the people, and went up, he and the elders of Israel, before the people to Ai.

verses.rationale: Preserves the north camp and singular him as Joshua rather than merging camp and ambush positions.
verses.before: All the people of war who were with him went up, drew near, and came before the city. They camped north of Ai, with the valley between them and Ai.
verses.after: All the fighting men with him advanced and came in front of the city. They camped north of Ai, with the valley between Joshua and Ai.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the people of war who were with him went up, drew near, and came before the city. They camped north of Ai, with the valley between them and Ai.

verses.rationale: Retains the approximate five thousand as a separate textual notice without inventing its relation to the thirty thousand.
verses.before: He took about five thousand men and set them in ambush between Bethel and Ai, west of the city.
verses.after: He took about five thousand men and placed them in ambush between Bethel and Ai, west of the city.
verses.tsw_comparator: He took about five thousand men and set them in ambush between Bethel and Ai, west of the city.

verses.rationale: Preserves the deployment summary and night notice in place; rear detachment renders the difficult heel/rear term with a note.
verses.before: So the people set the entire camp that was north of the city and its rear guard west of the city. Joshua went that night into the midst of the valley.
verses.after: The people positioned the whole camp north of the city and its rear detachment west of the city. That night Joshua went into the valley.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the people set the entire camp that was north of the city and its rear guard west of the city. Joshua went that night into the midst of the valley.

verses.rationale: Renders moed as appointed place, notes time alternative, and retains the king’s lack of knowledge.
verses.before: When the king of Ai saw it, the men of the city hurried and rose early and went out toward Israel for battle, he and all his people, at the appointed place before the Arabah. But he did not know that there was an ambush against him behind the city.
verses.after: When the king of Ai saw this, he and all his people hurried out early to fight Israel at the appointed place facing the Arabah. He did not know there was an ambush behind the city.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the king of Ai saw it, the men of the city hurried and rose early and went out toward Israel for battle, he and all his people, at the appointed place before the Arabah. But he did not know that there was an ambush against him behind the city.

verses.rationale: Expresses the planned apparent defeat in context without implying the ambush strategy failed.
verses.before: Joshua and all Israel allowed themselves to be struck before them and fled by the way of the wilderness.
verses.after: Joshua and all Israel let themselves be driven back and fled along the wilderness road.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua and all Israel allowed themselves to be struck before them and fled by the way of the wilderness.

verses.rationale: Follows qere in Ai and preserves the fulfillment of the drawing-away plan.
verses.before: All the people who were in the city were called together to pursue them. They pursued Joshua and were drawn away from the city.
verses.after: All the people in Ai were called out to pursue them. They chased Joshua and were drawn away from the city.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the people who were in the city were called together to pursue them. They pursued Joshua and were drawn away from the city.

verses.rationale: Retains Bethel’s presence in the pinned Hebrew and the unguarded city; does not silently remove the difficult name.
verses.before: Not a man remained in Ai or Bethel who did not go out after Israel. They left the city open and pursued Israel.
verses.after: Not a man remained in Ai or Bethel who did not go out after Israel. They left the city open and pursued Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Not a man remained in Ai or Bethel who did not go out after Israel. They left the city open and pursued Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps javelin as the distinct weapon and the repeated command/act with hand language.
verses.before: Then the LORD said to Joshua, “Stretch out the javelin that is in your hand toward Ai, for I will give it into your hand.” So Joshua stretched out the javelin that was in his hand toward the city.
verses.after: The LORD told Joshua, “Stretch out the javelin in your hand toward Ai, for I will give the city into your hand.” Joshua stretched out the javelin he held toward the city.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said to Joshua, “Stretch out the javelin that is in your hand toward Ai, for I will give it into your hand.” So Joshua stretched out the javelin that was in his hand toward the city.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the ambush force as actor and retains the signal followed by rapid capture and burning.
verses.before: The ambush rose quickly from its place. They ran as soon as he stretched out his hand, entered the city, captured it, and hurried to set the city on fire.
verses.after: The ambush force sprang from its position and ran as soon as he stretched out his hand. They entered the city, captured it, and quickly set it on fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: The ambush rose quickly from its place. They ran as soon as he stretched out his hand, entered the city, captured it, and hurried to set the city on fire.

verses.rationale: Keeps rising smoke and renders no hands to flee as inability, with a lexical note preserving the underlying image.
verses.before: The men of Ai turned back and looked, and look, the smoke of the city was going up toward heaven. They had no place to flee this way or that, for the people who had fled toward the wilderness turned back against the pursuers.
verses.after: The men of Ai looked back and saw smoke from the city rising toward heaven. They had no power to flee this way or that, for the people who had been fleeing toward the wilderness turned on their pursuers.
verses.tsw_comparator: The men of Ai turned back and looked, and behold, the smoke of the city was going up toward heaven. They had no place to flee this way or that, for the people who had fled toward the wilderness turned back against the pursuers.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated turnback report and the two signs prompting it.
verses.before: When Joshua and all Israel saw that the ambush had captured the city and that the smoke of the city went up, they turned back and struck the men of Ai.
verses.after: When Joshua and all Israel saw that the ambush force had captured the city and that its smoke was rising, they turned back and struck the men of Ai.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Joshua and all Israel saw that the ambush had captured the city and that the smoke of the city went up, they turned back and struck the men of Ai.

verses.rationale: Makes the converging forces intelligible and keeps the totalizing survivor/fugitive claim.
verses.before: The others came out from the city against them, so they were among Israel, some on this side and some on that side. Israel struck them until no survivor or fugitive was left.
verses.after: The men from the city came out against them too, trapping Ai’s men between Israel’s forces on either side. They struck them down until no survivor or fugitive was left.
verses.tsw_comparator: The others came out from the city against them, so they were in the midst of Israel, some on this side and some on that side. Israel struck them until no survivor or fugitive was left.

verses.rationale: Preserves the king’s temporary exception to the killing and his delivery alive.
verses.before: But they captured the king of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.
verses.after: They captured the king of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.
verses.tsw_comparator: But they captured the king of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.

verses.rationale: Retains the exhaustive killing outside and inside the city rather than reducing it to a battle victory.
verses.before: When Israel had finished killing all the inhabitants of Ai in the field, in the wilderness where they pursued them, and all of them had fallen by the edge of the sword until they were consumed, all Israel returned to Ai and struck it with the edge of the sword.
verses.after: Israel finished killing all Ai’s inhabitants in the open country, in the wilderness where they had pursued Israel. Every one of them fell by the sword. Then all Israel returned to Ai and put the city to the sword.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Israel had finished killing all the inhabitants of Ai in the field, in the wilderness where they pursued them, and all of them had fallen by the edge of the sword until they were consumed, all Israel returned to Ai and struck it with the edge of the sword.

verses.rationale: Keeps the exact twelve thousand and explicitly includes women in the stated total.
verses.before: Everyone who fell that day, men and women, were twelve thousand, all the people of Ai.
verses.after: All who fell that day, men and women, numbered twelve thousand—all the people of Ai.
verses.tsw_comparator: All who fell that day, men and women, were twelve thousand, all the people of Ai.

verses.rationale: Preserves the sustained gesture, Joshua’s agency, and herem’s full human scope.
verses.before: Joshua did not draw back his hand with which he stretched out the javelin until he had devoted all the inhabitants of Ai to destruction.
verses.after: Joshua did not draw back the hand holding his outstretched javelin until he had devoted all Ai’s inhabitants to destruction.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua did not draw back his hand with which he stretched out the javelin until he had devoted all the inhabitants of Ai to destruction.

verses.rationale: Keeps the plunder exception as fulfillment of verse 2 and names its authorization.
verses.before: Only the livestock and the plunder of that city Israel took for themselves, according to the word of the LORD that he had commanded Joshua.
verses.after: Israel took only the livestock and the city’s plunder for themselves, just as the LORD had commanded Joshua.
verses.tsw_comparator: Only the livestock and the plunder of that city Israel took for themselves, according to the word of the LORD that he had commanded Joshua.

verses.rationale: Retains permanent ruin and narrator’s present-day notice.
verses.before: Joshua burned Ai and made it a permanent mound, a desolation to this day.
verses.after: Joshua burned Ai and made it a permanent mound of ruins, a desolate place to this day.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua burned Ai and made it a permanent mound, a desolation to this day.

verses.rationale: Preserves tree, corpse, sunset removal, and memorial heap without specifying an unmentioned execution technique.
verses.before: He hanged the king of Ai on a tree until evening. At sunset Joshua commanded, and they took his corpse down from the tree, threw it at the entrance of the city gate, and raised over it a great heap of stones that remains to this day.
verses.after: He hung the king of Ai on a tree until evening. At sunset Joshua ordered the body taken down from the tree. They threw it at the entrance to the city gate and raised a great heap of stones over it, which remains to this day.
verses.tsw_comparator: He hanged the king of Ai on a tree until evening. At sunset Joshua commanded, and they took his corpse down from the tree, threw it at the entrance of the city gate, and raised over it a great heap of stones that remains to this day.

verses.rationale: Keeps the transition to worship at named Ebal and continues into the Mosaic instruction.
verses.before: Then Joshua built an altar to the LORD, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal,
verses.after: Then Joshua built an altar on Mount Ebal to the LORD, the God of Israel,
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Joshua built an altar to the LORD, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal,

verses.rationale: Preserves whole untooled stones, written authority, and both distinct offering types.
verses.before: as Moses, servant of the LORD, had commanded the children of Israel, as it is written in the book of the instruction of Moses: an altar of uncut stones upon which no iron tool had been wielded. They offered burnt offerings upon it to the LORD and sacrificed offerings of well-being.
verses.after: as Moses, the LORD’s servant, had commanded the Israelites. As written in the scroll of Moses’ instruction, it was an altar of whole stones on which no iron tool had been used. They offered burnt offerings to the LORD on it and sacrificed peace offerings.
verses.tsw_comparator: as Moses, servant of the LORD, had commanded the children of Israel, as it is written in the book of the instruction of Moses: an altar of uncut stones upon which no iron tool had been wielded. They offered burnt offerings upon it to the LORD and sacrificed offerings of well-being.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the repeated writing clause as Joshua’s public inscription without speculating on the copy’s length.
verses.before: There, on the stones, Joshua wrote a copy of the instruction of Moses that he had written before the children of Israel.
verses.after: There, in the sight of the Israelites, Joshua wrote on the stones a copy of Moses’ instruction.
verses.tsw_comparator: There, on the stones, Joshua wrote a copy of the instruction of Moses that he had written before the children of Israel.

verses.rationale: Unfolds the long assembly description while preserving officials, priestly carriers, resident foreigners, both mountains, and Mosaic command.
verses.before: All Israel, their elders, officers, and judges stood on both sides of the ark before the Levitical priests who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, the resident alien as well as the native-born. Half of them were in front of Mount Gerizim and half in front of Mount Ebal, as Moses, servant of the LORD, had commanded at first, to bless the people of Israel.
verses.after: All Israel, with its elders, officers, and judges, stood on both sides of the ark, facing the Levitical priests who carried the ark of the LORD’s covenant. Resident foreigners and native-born Israelites stood together: half faced Mount Gerizim, and half faced Mount Ebal, as Moses, the LORD’s servant, had first commanded for blessing the people of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: All Israel, their elders, officers, and judges stood on both sides of the ark before the Levitical priests who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, the resident alien as well as the native-born. Half of them were in front of Mount Gerizim and half in front of Mount Ebal, as Moses, servant of the LORD, had commanded at first, to bless the people of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains comprehensive reading and both blessing and curse, linking instruction to chapter 1.
verses.before: Afterward Joshua read all the words of the instruction, the blessing and the curse, according to all that is written in the book of the instruction.
verses.after: Afterward Joshua read all the words of the instruction—the blessing and the curse—everything written in the scroll of instruction.
verses.tsw_comparator: Afterward Joshua read all the words of the instruction, the blessing and the curse, according to all that is written in the book of the instruction.

verses.rationale: Preserves the emphatic completeness and all specifically named listeners instead of letting all Israel obscure them.
verses.before: There was not a word of all that Moses commanded that Joshua did not read before all the assembly of Israel, including the women, the little children, and the resident aliens who lived among them.
verses.after: Not one word of all Moses had commanded was left unread by Joshua before the whole assembly of Israel, including the women, the little ones, and the resident foreigners who lived among them.
verses.tsw_comparator: There was not a word of all that Moses commanded that Joshua did not read before all the assembly of Israel, including the women, the little children, and the resident aliens who lived among them.
